issues.description: The solution declares the Bookstore's books property as `private let books: [Book]` (Solution: Bookstore.swift lines 9-16), but Client.swift iterates over `bookstore.books` (Solution: Client.swift lines 10-11). In Swift, `private` restricts access to the enclosing declaration/file and prevents other source files in the same module from accessing the property. This mismatch will cause a compilation error and prevents the Client from accessing the books as shown in the solution. The problem statement expects a Bookstore that "holds an array of `Book`s named `books`" and shows client code that accesses that array (Problem Statement lines 8-12 and 31-38), so the `private` visibility on the property is inconsistent with the intended usage.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the books property accessible to Client by removing the `private` modifier (e.g. `let books: [Book]`) or by using an appropriate access level such as `internal`/`public` depending on intended encapsulation. Alternatively provide a public accessor or method on Bookstore to expose the books collection. This will align the implementation with the problem statement and the Client usage.
